historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 5yr CAGR 7.2% and EPS 5yr CAGR 13.0% both exceed the 3.7% equity CAGR by far more than 30%. Equity growth is suppressed by ~JPY120bn of buybacks and dividends over FY2022-26 and by the FY2024 loss; EPS CAGR is inflated by FY2026's 88bn securities sale gains and a 9% lower share count, and the 3yr EPS CAGR (41%) is off the near-zero FY2023 base. None of these is a forward growth rate; the forward paths are set from guidance and mid-cycle margins, not from any CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: owner FCF (reported FCF less interest and dividend income, SBC nil) was -47.9bn in FY2021, +9.3bn in FY2023 and -66.6bn in FY2026 -- negative at both endpoints of the 5yr window and at the 3yr endpoint. Ten-year cumulative reported FCF FY2017-26 ~68bn vs cumulative net income ~767bn: earnings have been reinvested in income real estate and working capital rather than converted to free cash. Revenue CAGRs: FY2023->FY2026 2,057,802/1,933,814; FY2021->FY2026 2,057,802/1,456,473. Equity: owners' equity 977,977 (Mar-2026) vs 852,559 (Mar-2023) and 815,288 (Mar-2021). EPS 186.68 vs 66.29 and 101.17.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle normalisation: FY2027 guidance (EBITDA ~8.1%) is largely delivered at 7.8%, then the margin fades to a 6.8% mid-cycle level as the current cohort of large projects passes its peak-profitability stage; revenue grows 12% in the guided year (incl. Aomi) then at 1.5-3% nominal. Owner FCF runs ~1.7-2.3% of sales because income-property capex (3.0-3.5%) exceeds D&A (1.7%) and growth consumes working capital. Terminal value capped at 12x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: FY2027 margin is the new normal (8.0% EBITDA sustained), AI/data-centre and redevelopment demand keeps volumes compounding 3-5% for several years and the Big-5 hold pricing discipline. Same WACC and capex as base.
scenario_narratives.bear: A milder repeat of the FY2024 loss episode in years 2-3 (EBITDA trough 3.5%, revenue -7% cumulative), with recovery only to the 5.2% five-year average; investment curtailed; terminal growth 0.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A going-concern owner-FCF DCF on a Big-5 Japanese general contractor, normalised to mid-cycle margins rather than extrapolated from either the FY2024 loss or the FY2026-27 peak. The flows exclude every FY2026/Q1 FY2027 one-off (88bn cross-shareholding sale gain, 5.9bn and 35.8bn negative-goodwill gains, 11.8bn Q1 securities gain) by construction, because they are non-operating; their source assets (357bn of investment securities, less deferred tax) are credited in the bridge instead. Shimizu converts earnings to free cash poorly -- ten-year cumulative FCF ~9% of cumulative net income -- because it reinvests in income real estate and working capital, and the model charges that reinvestment. The result sits well below the earnings- and book-multiple values the market pays, which is the finding: the share price credits the real-estate reinvestment at roughly book, this model credits only projected cash. Price/value should be read alongside P/B (~1.4x) and the 12x FCF terminal cap, which binds in every scenario and makes terminal growth nearly irrelevant.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex assumption is the dominant driver: every 0.5pp of sales of capex (~12bn/yr) is worth roughly JPY150-180/share. If the income-property programme is scaled back and proceeds recycled to shareholders (as the cross-shareholding sell-down already is), the owner-FCF value rises sharply toward the P/B-implied value.
Recurrence of an FY2024-style cost-overrun/quality-defect episode (reserve for expected losses still 54.9bn; EY key audit matter on total-cost estimation) -- the bear case, weighted 25%.
Peak-cycle margin: FY2027 OI guidance (6.6%) is explicitly attributed to large projects at their most profitable stage; base fades to 6.8% EBITDA and bull assumes 8.0% is durable.

Real-estate development cash flows are lumpy (receivables +130.7bn in FY2026; 'real estate and other' gross profit 37-54bn/yr), so any single year's reported FCF is a poor guide; the component build and the working-capital capture are judgments.

Investment-securities bridge (300bn, ~JPY440/share) assumes the cross-shareholdings are realisable near fair value less tax; the Seiwa Building equity-method stake is carried at a book value that includes a 35.8bn negative-goodwill step-up.

Labour: Japan's construction workforce is shrinking and capped by the April-2024 overtime rules; subcontractors are turning down work, so volume growth above ~2% nominal may be unattainable regardless of demand.
Interest-rate normalisation in Japan raises the cost of the 573bn debt stack and could cool private building investment; the intraday price used here may differ from the regular close.

inputs.net_debt_note: 2026-06-30 consolidated BS (1803.T_Quarterly_Q1-FY2026.txt:458-511): cash 348,847 + negotiable CDs held as marketable securities 85,000 = 433,847 (this matches the cash-flow statement's cash-equivalents definition: at 2026-03-31 cash 237,992 + NCDs 118,000 = 355,992 vs CF cash equivalents 354,492). Debt = short-term borrowings 243,391 + current non-recourse 3,625 + current bonds 10,000 + bonds 156,000 + non-recourse bonds 450 + long-term borrowings 129,443 + non-recourse borrowings 30,303 = 573,212. Non-recourse project debt (JPY34.4bn) is included as debt; its assets sit in tangible fixed assets whose rental income is inside the flows. Lease liabilities are not in debt (see lease_treatment).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows, and identical across the three scenarios (risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate). Cost of equity ~7.7% = 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct 2026) + beta ~1.0 x Japan ERP 6.0%. After-tax cost of debt ~1.0% (FY2026 interest expense 7,569 on ~570bn debt = 1.3% pre-tax). Debt is ~29% of market-value capital, so the mechanical WACC is ~5.8%; rounded up to 7.0% because a 1.0 market beta understates project/claim risk on fixed-price contracts, and to match the sibling zenekon builds (1801.T Taisei 7.0%, 1802.T Obayashi 7.5%) so the Big-5 set is comparable. Terminal growth 1.0% base (Japanese nominal GDP with a shrinking construction workforce); terminal cap 12x FCF for a cyclical contractor (method: 12-15x for cyclicals), which binds in every scenario at a 7% WACC.
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP filer: operating leases are expensed inside cost of sales/SG&A, so the lease cost is already in the EBITDA margin (treatment B, no separate lease line). Finance-lease liabilities are immaterial (nonconsolidated 1,049 current + 8,629 non-current at 2026-03-31) and are excluded from net debt. Charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (operating-income based). Non-controlling interests of JPY14,410m at 2026-06-30 are deducted ONCE in the equity bridge. NCI shrank from 63,844 (Mar-2025) to 23,198 (Mar-2026) to 14,410 (Jun-2026) after the group spent JPY55.4bn in FY2026 buying out a subsidiary minority; NCI took only 2,837 of FY2026 profit and 153 in Q1 FY2027, so attributable and consolidated flows are now within 2% of each other.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'; owner-fcf.md and owner-fcf-adaptations.md read in full: JPY WACC, J-GAAP leases, NCI charged once, matching-asset bridge, SBC-zero, risk charged once). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. EBITDA = operating income + depreciation (DB convention; FY2026 118,669 + 33,511 = 152,180, 7.4% of sales). KEY JUDGMENT -- MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION, NOT EXTRAPOLATION OF EITHER EXTREME: FY2024 (year to Mar-2024) was an operating LOSS of 24.7bn from cost overruns and quality defects on several super-large projects; FY2025 recovered to 3.7% OI margin, FY2026 to 5.8%, and FY2027 guidance (maintained 2026-07-30) is OI 153.0bn on sales 2,310bn = 6.6% (EBITDA ~8.1%), which management attributes to large projects reaching their PEAK profitability stage plus secured change orders -- i.e. a cyclical high, not a run-rate. Ten-year EBITDA margin history: FY2017-21 8.0-9.0%, FY2022-23 4.2-4.4%, FY2024 0.3%, FY2025 5.4%, FY2026 7.4%; ten-year average 6.5%. Base case therefore takes FY2027 EBITDA at 7.8% (a small execution haircut to the 8.1% guidance) and fades to 6.8% by year 5 -- a little above the ten-year average, crediting the post-2024 contract reforms (inflation sliding-scale clauses, change-order compensation, order screening) but not the peak. FY2026 ONE-OFFS ARE OUTSIDE THE FLOWS BY CONSTRUCTION: the 88.2bn gain on sale of cross-shareholdings, the 5.9bn negative goodwill, the Q1 FY2027 35.8bn Seiwa Building negative-goodwill/equity-method gain and the 11.8bn Q1 securities gain are all non-operating or special items; the flows are built from operating income, and the source assets (investment securities) are carried in the bridge instead (matching-asset rule). REPORTED FCF IS NOT THE BASE: FY2026 reported FCF was -57.0bn (OCF 41.6bn after a 130.7bn receivables build on March completions; capex 98.7bn in a heavy real-estate-development year). Ten-year cumulative reported FCF FY2017-26 is only ~68bn against ~767bn of cumulative net income because Shimizu reinvests most earnings into income real estate (tangible fixed assets 662bn at Jun-2026) and working capital. The component build charges that reinvestment: capex 3.5% of sales fading to 3.0% (five-year average 4.1%, ten-year 4.6%, but FY2020-22 included an unusually large development programme) against D&A 1.6% rising to 1.7%; working capital -5% of incremental revenue (receivables + uncompleted costs exceed advances + payables by ~340bn at Jun-2026, so growth consumes cash). This is why the owner-FCF value sits well below what P/E or P/B would imply, and the same is true of the sibling builds (1801.T, 1802.T): the market credits the real-estate reinvestment at roughly book; this model credits only the cash it is projected to throw off. CASH TAX 30.5% flat (Japanese statutory ~30.6%; FY2026 cash tax 33.6bn on ~122bn ordinary income = 27.5%, with 45.5bn payable at year-end on the securities gain -- no NOL or one-off credit to ramp). BRIDGE: see equity_bridge. Pension: net defined benefit liability 21,835 less asset 2,403 (Mar-2026) = 19,432, after tax ~13,500, deducted.

bear.narrative: FY2027 lands a little under guidance (7.0% EBITDA), then the FY2024 pattern recurs in milder form: the 54.9bn reserve for expected losses on contracts in process proves insufficient as labour-cost inflation and the 2024 overtime cap squeeze fixed-price backlog, a cluster of large projects slips, and EBITDA falls to 3.5% in year 3 while revenue contracts 4% and 3% as management again prioritises screening over volume (the FY2025 playbook). Recovery is to 5.2% -- the FY2022-26 five-year average, not the FY2017-20 level -- on the view that project-management discipline has not structurally improved. Investment is curtailed (capex 2.5%) and terminal growth is 0.5%.

base.narrative: Year 1 follows the maintained FY2027 guidance (sales +12.3% to 2,310bn incl. Aomi Construction; OI 153bn = 6.6%, EBITDA ~8.1%) with a small execution haircut to 7.8%. Thereafter revenue grows at Japanese nominal rates (3% then 2% fading to 1.5%: book-to-bill 1.05x on FY2026 orders of 2,159bn supports FY2027, but labour capacity caps volume) and the EBITDA margin fades from the peak-stage 7.8% to a 6.8% mid-cycle level, slightly above the 6.5% ten-year average to credit the sliding-scale/change-order contract reforms. Capex 3.5% fading to 3.0% of sales keeps the income-property programme running at roughly its five-year pace; D&A drifts up to 1.7%.

bull.narrative: Guidance is met in full and the FY2027 margin proves to be the new normal rather than a peak: the contract reforms hold, the Big-5 oligopoly keeps pricing discipline on data-centre, semiconductor-fab, Tokyo/Osaka redevelopment and National Resilience public works, and EBITDA settles at 8.0% (the FY2017-20 level). Revenue compounds 4-5% for three years on the AI/data-centre capex wave and overseas bolt-ons before fading to 2%. Same capex and WACC as base: the bull axis is margin durability and volume, not a cheaper discount rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the FY2024 operating loss was company-specific (worse than Taisei/Obayashi/Kajima in the same cost cycle), the reserve for expected losses on contracts in process is still JPY54.9bn, EY flags total-cost estimation as a key audit matter, and management itself describes FY2027 as large projects reaching PEAK profitability. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it requires both that the reforms make 8% EBITDA durable AND that the data-centre/fab capex wave outruns the labour-capacity ceiling. Matches the 25/50/25 used on sibling 1801.T; 1802.T used 30/50/20.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
